A system of fluid passages in the inner ear, including both the cochlea, which is part of the auditory system, and the vestibular system, which provides the sense of balance. The bony labyrinth, or osseous labyrinth, is the network of passages with bony walls lined with periosteum. The bony labyrinth is lined with the membranous labyrinth. There is a layer of perilymph between them. The three parts of the bony labyrinth are the vestibule of the ear, the semicircular canals, and the cochlea. The vestibular system is the region of the inner ear where the semicircular canals converge, close to the cochlea (the hearing organ). The vestibular system works with the visual system to keep objects in focus when the head is moving. Joint and muscle receptors also are important in maintaining balance. The brain receives, interprets, and processes the information from these systems that control our balance. [WP,unvetted].
definition.es: Sistema de conductos llenos de líquido del oído interno, que comprende tanto la cóclea, que forma parte del sistema auditivo, como el sistema vestibular, que proporciona el sentido del equilibrio. El laberinto óseo es la red de conductos con paredes óseas revestidas de periostio. El laberinto óseo está revestido por el laberinto membranoso. Entre ambos hay una capa de perilinfa. Las tres partes del laberinto óseo son el vestíbulo del oído, los conductos semicirculares y la cóclea. El sistema vestibular es la región del oído interno donde convergen los conductos semicirculares, cerca de la cóclea (el órgano de la audición). El sistema vestibular actúa junto con el sistema visual para mantener los objetos enfocados cuando la cabeza se mueve. Los receptores articulares y musculares también son importantes para mantener el equilibrio. El encéfalo recibe, interpreta y procesa la información de estos sistemas que controlan nuestro equilibrio. [WP,unvetted].

Vertebra prominens is the proper name for the seventh cervical vertebra. The most distinctive characteristic of this vertebra is the existence of a long and prominent spinous process which is palpable from the skin surface, hence the name. This spinous process is thick, nearly horizontal in direction, not bifurcated, but terminating in a tubercle to which the lower end of the ligamentum nuchae is attached. The seventh cervical vertebra (C7) has the most prominent spinous process only in about 70% of people; in the remainder, either C6 or T1 (the first thoracic vertebra) will be the most prominent. The transverse processes are of considerable size, their posterior roots are large and prominent, while the anterior are small and faintly marked; the upper surface of each has usually a shallow sulcus for the eighth spinal nerve, and its extremity seldom presents more than a trace of bifurcation. The foramen transversarium may be as large as that in the other cervical vertebrae, but is generally smaller on one or both sides; occasionally it is double, sometimes it is absent. On the left side it occasionally gives passage to the vertebral artery; more frequently the vertebral vein traverses it on both sides; but the usual arrangement is for both artery and vein to pass in front of the transverse process, and not through the foramen. Sometimes the anterior root of the transverse process attains a large size and exists as a separate bone, which is known as a cervical rib.
definition.es: Vértebra prominente es el nombre propio de la séptima vértebra cervical. La característica más distintiva de esta vértebra es la existencia de una apófisis espinosa larga y prominente, palpable desde la superficie cutánea, de ahí su nombre. Esta apófisis espinosa es gruesa, de dirección casi horizontal, no bífida, sino que termina en un tubérculo al que se fija el extremo inferior del ligamento nucal. La séptima vértebra cervical (C7) tiene la apófisis espinosa más prominente solo en alrededor del 70 % de las personas; en el resto, la más prominente será C6 o T1 (la primera vértebra torácica). Las apófisis transversas son de tamaño considerable; sus raíces posteriores son grandes y prominentes, mientras que las anteriores son pequeñas y poco marcadas; la cara superior de cada una presenta habitualmente un surco poco profundo para el octavo nervio espinal, y su extremo rara vez presenta más que un vestigio de bifurcación. El agujero transverso puede ser tan grande como el de las demás vértebras cervicales, pero generalmente es más pequeño en uno o ambos lados; en ocasiones es doble y a veces falta. En el lado izquierdo da paso ocasionalmente a la arteria vertebral; con más frecuencia lo atraviesa la vena vertebral en ambos lados; pero la disposición habitual es que tanto la arteria como la vena pasen por delante de la apófisis transversa y no a través del agujero. A veces la raíz anterior de la apófisis transversa alcanza un gran tamaño y existe como un hueso separado, que se conoce como costilla cervical.

The superior mesenteric plexus is a continuation of the lower part of the celiac plexus, receiving a branch from the junction of the right vagus nerve with the plexus. It surrounds the superior mesenteric artery, accompanies it into the mesentery, and divides into a number of secondary plexuses, which are distributed to all the parts supplied by the artery, viz. , pancreatic branches to the pancreas; intestinal branches to the small intestine; and ileocolic, right colic, and middle colic branches, which supply the corresponding parts of the great intestine. The nerves composing this plexus are white in color and firm in texture; in the upper part of the plexus close to the origin of the superior mesenteric artery is the superior mesenteric ganglion.

On the external surface of the optic choroid is a thin membrane, the suprachoroid lamina, composed of delicate non-vascular lamellae-each lamella consisting of a network of fine elastic fibers among which are branched pigment cells.
definition.es: En la cara externa de la coroides hay una membrana delgada, la lámina supracoroidea, compuesta por laminillas delicadas no vasculares; cada laminilla consiste en una red de finas fibras elásticas entre las que hay células pigmentarias ramificadas.

definition.en: A bone that is shaped as a broad flat plate and composed of two thin layers of compact tissue enclosing between them a variable quantity of cancellous tissue, which is the location of red bone marrow.

The subdivision of the skeleton that consists of all the skeletal elements at the distalmost end of the manual autopodium - i.e. the bones of the hands or their cartilaginous precursors[VSAO,modified].

synonymsEn: pelvic girdle plus pelvic limb or fin
pelvic girdle plus posterior limb or fin

definition.en: Appendage girdle complex that when present, encompasses the pelvic appendicular skeleton and the pelvic girdle.

The anterior digastric is a pharyngeal arch I muscle that participates in oral/pharygeal behaviors and is innervated by the nerve to mylohyoid (a branch of the third division of the trigeminal nerve), is attached to the mandible and to the hyoid apparatus, and it is superficial to mylohyoid muscle.
definition.es: El digástrico anterior es un músculo del arco faríngeo I que participa en conductas orales/faríngeas, está inervado por el nervio del milohioideo (un ramo de la tercera división del nervio trigémino), se fija a la mandíbula y al aparato hioideo y es superficial al músculo milohioideo.

definition.en: An epiphysis that is part of a metacarpal bone of digit 5.

The ora serrata is the serrated junction between the retina and the ciliary body. This junction marks the transition from the simple non-photosensitive area of the retina to the complex, multi-layered photosensitive region. In animals in which the region does not have a serrated appearance, it is called the ora ciliaris retinae.
definition.es: La ora serrata es la unión dentada entre la retina y el cuerpo ciliar. Esta unión marca la transición desde la zona simple no fotosensible de la retina hasta la región fotosensible compleja y multiestratificada. En los animales en los que esta región no tiene aspecto dentado, se denomina ora ciliaris retinae.

synonymsEn: digastric branch of facial nerve (CN VII)
nerve to posterior belly of digastric

definition.en: The digastric branch of facial nerve arises close to the stylomastoid foramen, and divides into several filaments, which supply the posterior belly of the Digastricus; one of these filaments joins the glossopharyngeal nerve.
definition.es: El ramo digástrico del nervio facial se origina cerca del agujero estilomastoideo y se divide en varios filamentos, que inervan el vientre posterior del digástrico; uno de estos filamentos se une al nervio glosofaríngeo.

definition.en: The styloid process of the ulna projects from the medial and back part of the bone; it descends a little lower than the head, and its rounded end affords attachment to the ulnar collateral ligament of the wrist[WP,unvetted].

UBERON:0011979.labelEn: epiphysis of distal phalanx of manus
synonymsEn: epiphysis of distal phalanx of finger

definition.en: An epiphysis that is part of a distal phalanx of manus.

The Buccal fat pad is one of several encapsulated fat masses in the cheek. It is a deep fat pad located on either side of the face between the buccinator muscle and several more superficial muscles. It should not be confused with the malar fat pad, which is directly below the skin of the cheek. It should also not be confused with jowl fat pads. It is implicated in the formation of hollow cheeks and the nasolabial fold, but not in the formation of jowls.
definition.es: El cuerpo adiposo bucal es una de varias masas de grasa encapsuladas de la mejilla. Es un cuerpo adiposo profundo situado a cada lado de la cara, entre el músculo buccinador y varios músculos más superficiales. No debe confundirse con el cuerpo adiposo malar, que se encuentra directamente bajo la piel de la mejilla. Tampoco debe confundirse con los cuerpos adiposos de la papada. Interviene en la formación de las mejillas hundidas y del surco nasolabial, pero no en la formación de la papada.

synonymsEn: valve of fossa navicularis of urethra

definition.en: An inconstant fold or valve of mucous membrane sometimes found in the root or upper wall of the navicular fossa of the urethra.

relations.labelEn: navicular fossa of spongiose part of urethra

definition.en: The anterior cervical lymph nodes are a group of nodes found on the anterior part of the neck.
definition.es: Los nódulos linfáticos cervicales anteriores son un grupo de nódulos situados en la parte anterior del cuello.

definition.en: The small area behind the wisdom teeth.

UBERON:0012398.labelEn: large intestine smooth muscle circular layer

definition.en: A circular muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a large intestine smooth muscle.

isA.labelEn: circular muscle layer of muscular coat

definition.en: The deep cervical fascia (or fascia colli in older texts) lies under cover of the Platysma, and invests the neck; it also forms sheaths for the carotid vessels, and for the structures situated in front of the vertebral column. Its attachment to the hyoid bone prevents the formation of a dewlap. The investing portion of the fascia is attached behind to the ligamentum nucha and to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra. The 'alar fascia' is a portion of deep cervical fascia.
definition.es: La fascia cervical profunda (o fascia colli en textos antiguos) se sitúa bajo el platisma y envuelve el cuello; también forma vainas para los vasos carotídeos y para las estructuras situadas por delante de la columna vertebral. Su fijación al hueso hioides impide la formación de una papada. La porción de revestimiento de la fascia se fija por detrás al ligamento nucal y a la apófisis espinosa de la séptima vértebra cervical. La «fascia alar» es una porción de la fascia cervical profunda.

definition.en: A section through the tube or network of tubes that connects the ovaries to the outside of the body.

The Brodmann area 32, also known in the human brain as the dorsal anterior cingulate area 32, refers to a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined cingulate region of cerebral cortex. In the human it forms an outer arc around the anterior cingulate gyrus. The cingulate sulcus defines approximately its inner boundary and the superior rostral sulcus (H) its ventral boundary; rostrally it extends almost to the margin of the frontal lobe. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded internally by the ventral anterior cingulate area 24, externally by medial margins of the agranular frontal area 6, intermediate frontal area 8, granular frontal area 9, frontopolar area 10, and prefrontal area 11-1909. (Brodmann19-09). Dorsal region of anterior cingulate gyrus is associated with rational thought processes, most notably active during the Stroop task.
Anatomical space that is an opening in a bone of the skull.
definition.es: Espacio anatómico que es una abertura en un hueso del cráneo.

definition.en: A tubular passage that extends from the primitive pit into the head process during the early stages of embryonic development in mammals. It perforates the splanchnopleure layer so that the yolk sac and the amnion are connected temporarily.
A metaphysis that is part of a ulna.

UBERON:0014507.labelEn: distal interphalangeal joint of pedal digit 3
synonymsEn: distal interphalangeal joint of pedal digit III
distal interphalangeal joint of third digit of foot
distal interphalangeal joint of third toe

definition.en: A distal inter-phalangeal joint that is part of the 3rd pedal digit.

synonymsEn: left crus of lumbar part of diaphragm

definition.en: A crus of diaphragm that is in_the_left_side_of a diaphragm.
definition.es: Pilar del diafragma que se encuentra en el lado izquierdo de un diafragma.

definition.en: This is the point at which the trachea splits into two (left and right) principal bronchi. It is located in the region of the fourth to sixth intercostal space, though this varies with species and with respiratory phase. This position closely associates the bifurcation with the heart base. The thickened median crest initiating the bifurcation is called the tracheal carina .

UBERON:0015786.labelEs: región respiratoria de la mucosa nasal

definition.en: The portion of the nasal mucosa that is part of the respiratory system.
definition.es: Porción de la mucosa nasal que forma parte del aparato respiratorio.

definition.en: A lymph node along the left gastric artery or greater omentum.
definition.es: Nódulo linfático situado a lo largo de la arteria gástrica izquierda o del omento mayor.

definition.en: The internal iliac lymph nodes (or hypogastric) surround the internal iliac artery and its branches (the hypogastric vessels), and receive the lymphatics corresponding to the distribution of the branches of it, i. e. , they receive lymphatics from all the pelvic viscera, from the deeper parts of the perineum, including the membranous and cavernous portions of the urethra, and from the buttock and back of the thigh. It does not receive lymph from the ovary, testis, or superior half of the rectum; the gonads drain to the paraaortic lymph nodes, while the superior half of the rectum drains to the pararectal lymph nodes.
definition.es: Los nódulos linfáticos ilíacos internos (o hipogástricos) rodean la arteria ilíaca interna y sus ramas (los vasos hipogástricos) y reciben los linfáticos correspondientes a la distribución de sus ramas, es decir, reciben linfáticos de todas las vísceras pélvicas, de las partes más profundas del periné, incluidas las porciones membranosa y cavernosa de la uretra, y de la nalga y la cara posterior del muslo. No recibe linfa del ovario, del testículo ni de la mitad superior del recto; las gónadas drenan en los nódulos linfáticos paraaórticos, mientras que la mitad superior del recto drena en los nódulos linfáticos pararrectales.

definition.en: A lymph node that is located close to the surface.

UBERON:0016404.labelEs: articulación de los arcos vertebrales cervicales
synonymsEn: joint of cervical vertebral articular process

definition.en: A vertebral arch joint that is part of a cervical region of vertebral column.
definition.es: Articulación de arco vertebral que forma parte de la región cervical de la columna vertebral.

synonymsEn: skin of orbital part of face

definition.en: A zone of skin in the periorbital region of the face.
definition.es: Zona de piel de la región periorbitaria de la cara.

definition.en: The parvocellular reticular nucleus is part of the brain located dorsolateral to the nucleus reticularis pontis caudalis. The dorsal portion of the reticular nucleus has been shown to innervate the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus and its surrounding area. Also, it projects to the facial nucleus, hypoglossal nucleus and parabrachial nucleus along with parts of the caudal parvocellular reticular formation. This nucleus is also involved in expiration with a part of the gigantocellular nucleus.
A frenulum of lip that is part of a upper lip.
definition.es: Frenillo labial que forma parte de un labio superior.

definition.en: Hypothenar refers to a group of three muscles of the palm that control the motion of the little finger. The three muscles are: Abductor digiti minimi Flexor digiti minimi Opponens digiti minimi.
A central point or region on the anterior or posterior surface of the lens.
definition.es: Punto o región central de la cara anterior o posterior del cristalino.

definition.en: A small conical elevation at the basal angle of the lacrimal lake.
definition.es: Pequeña elevación cónica situada en el ángulo basal del lago lagrimal.

definition.en: The inferior longitudinal fasciculus connects the temporal lobe and occipital lobe, running along the lateral walls of the inferior and posterior cornua of the lateral ventricle. The existence of this fasciculus independent from the occipitotemporal fasciculus has been questioned for the human being, such that it has been proposed that the term inferior longitudinal fasciculus be replaced by the term 'occipitotemporal projection'.
A cranial suture in the midline of the skull that connects the left and right maxilla bones.
definition.es: Sutura craneal situada en la línea media del cráneo que une los huesos maxilares izquierdo y derecho.

synonymsEn: lateral part of fornix of vagina

definition.en: The vaginal fornix that is to the side of the cervix.

UBERON:0034981.labelEn: superior bulb of internal jugular vein
UBERON:0034981.labelEs: bulbo superior de la vena yugular interna

synonymsEn: plantar metatarsal branch of plantar arch

definition.en: The plantar metatarsal arteries (digital branches) are four in number, and run forward between the metatarsal bones and in contact with the Interossei. Each divides into a pair of plantar digital arteries which supply the adjacent sides of the toes. Near their points of division each sends upward an anterior perforating branch to join the corresponding dorsal metatarsal artery. The first plantar metatarsal artery (arteria princeps hallucis) springs from the junction between the lateral plantar and deep plantar arteries and sends a digital branch to the medial side of the first toe. The digital branch for the lateral side of the fifth toe arise from the lateral plantar artery near the base of the fifth metatarsal bone.
Zone of esophagus located in the thorax.
The narrowest portion of the gallbladder and distal to the cystic duct.
definition.es: Porción más estrecha de la vesícula biliar, distal al conducto cístico.

definition.en: A small triangular process of dura matter beginning at the internal occipital crest just beneath the tentorium and projecting forward.
Clinical esophageal segment composed of skeletal muscle. It corresponds to the superior part of the upper third topographic segment of the esophagus.
The junction of the precentral gyrus and postcentral gyrus on the medial surface of the cerebral cortex. It lies across the boundary between the frontal lobe and the parietal lobe.

The Palmaris brevis is a thin, quadrilateral muscle, placed beneath the integument of the ulnar side of the hand. It arises by tendinous fasciculi from the transverse carpal ligament and palmar aponeurosis; the fleshy fibers are inserted into the skin on the ulnar border of the palm of the hand. The muscle is innervated by the superficial branch of the ulnar nerve, containing fibers from the eighth cervical and first thoracic nerves.

synonymsEn: pubic branch of inferior epigastric vein

definition.en: vein ascending the posterior aspect of the body of the pubis to drain into the inferior epigastric vein; this vein frequently (about 20% of patients) serves as an accessory or replaced obturator vein.

A vein that drains the prepuce and skin of the penis, and, running backward in the subcutaneous tissue, inclines to the right or left, and opens into the corresponding superficial external pudendal vein, a tributary of the great saphenous vein..

synonymsEn: anterior bronchopulmonary segment of left pulmonary artery
anterior segmental artery of left lung
anterior segmental artery of left upper lobe
skin of posterior part of leg

definition.en: Skin of the back of the lower leg.
A vein that is tributary of the segmental pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a subsegment of the lung.
definition.es: Vena que es tributaria de las venas pulmonares segmentarias y drena sangre oxigenada de un subsegmento del pulmón.

definition.en: An artery of the neck that branches from the external carotid artery and supplies the pharynx.
definition.es: Arteria del cuello que se origina de la arteria carótida externa e irriga la faringe.

definition.en: An artery that branches from the facial artery that runs forward under the mouth, then turns upward upon reaching the chin.
definition.es: Arteria que se origina de la arteria facial, discurre hacia delante por debajo de la boca y luego se dirige hacia arriba al llegar al mentón.

synonymsEn: Set of long posterior ciliary arteries

definition.en: An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the choroid, ciliary body and iris.

UBERON:8930047.labelEs: capa muscular interna del infundíbulo de la trompa uterina

definition.es: Capa componente de órgano compuesta principalmente por tejido muscular liso de disposición circular, que forma la capa más interna de la túnica muscular del infundíbulo de la trompa uterina y contribuye a las contracciones peristálticas que ayudan al transporte de los gametos y del embrión.
